jobs.description:
Would you like to shape the people, culture and organisational foundations of one of the world’s leading humanitarian organisations?  

This is an opportunity to bring your global leadership experience to a mission with profound human impact. As Executive Director for People & Organisation (P&O) at the Danish Refugee Council (DRC), you will inspire employees, empower leaders and turn strategy into meaningful change – ensuring that DRC has the people, capabilities, structures and safeguards required to deliver effective humanitarian responses wherever they are needed most. 
 

You will join DRC at an important time and have a real opportunity to influence its global direction and organisation. The global humanitarian system is going through fundamental change, and you will help shape and adapt organisational structure, operating models and staff capacity to the challenges and opportunities of the future. Your portfolio is global and spans organisation and culture, HR and leadership development, surge capacity, safety, legal affairs and Code of Conduct. As a member of the Executive Management Team, you will help shape strategy, and you will lead approximately 200 colleagues across P&O functions in headquarters and countries. 

About the job 

Reporting directly to the Secretary General, you will set the direction for DRC’s global People & Organisation strategy and ensure that it becomes an enabler for DRC’s ambitions. In close partnership with the Executive Management Team and senior leaders, you will create the conditions for talented people to grow and thrive – while strengthening an inclusive, and high-performing culture. 

This role calls for a leader who enjoys moving between strategic ambition and practical delivery. You will ensure that global policies, systems, data, employment conditions and governance provide relevant and timely support to operations. At the same time, you will carry executive accountability for safeguarding, ethical conduct, legal compliance, safety and DRC’s humanitarian surge capacity – areas fundamental to DRC’s mission. 

You will lead and develop an experienced senior team; Global HR, HR Denmark, HR Operations & Analytics, Surge Capacity, Safety, Code of Conduct, Legal, management support, and change, leadership and culture. Based at DRC’s headquarters in Copenhagen, you will work across a global organisation and build trusted relationships with colleagues and partners from many cultures and contexts. 

The impact you will make: 

• 
Shape DRC’s strategy, culture and global P&O agenda. 

• 
Lead organisational change, leadership development and employee engagement. 

• 
Attract, develop and retain the people DRC needs to deliver its mission. 

• 
Ensure effective global P&O policies, systems, services and people insights. 

• 
Oversee safeguarding, Code of Conduct, safety, legal compliance, duty of care. 

• 
Strengthen humanitarian surge capacity. 

About you 

You are a credible executive who is motivated by purpose and energised by complexity. You bring the strategic perspective to see the whole organisation, the judgement to make thoughtful choices and the drive to translate ambition into clear priorities and measurable results. Colleagues experience you as an inclusive and trusted leader with integrity and empathy providing the clarity to make decisions and create momentum. 
 

What you will bring: 

• 
10+ years of senior experience in global organisations and people leadership. 

• 
A strong record of shaping people strategy and leading transformation across complex, international operations. 

• 
Experience of organisational development, including the renewal and design of operating models. 

• 
Broad understanding of governance, compliance, safeguarding, safety and legal matters.

• 
Strong stakeholder management, analytical and communication skills. 

• 
An inclusive, decisive and high-integrity leadership style. 

• 
A relevant master’s degree and fluent English; additional competency in French, Spanish, Arabic and Danish are an advantage. 

All employees in DRC should master DRC's core competencies: Communicating, Taking the lead, Collaborating, Striving for excellence and Demonstrating integrity.
 

We offer 

Contract length: Permanent 

Work location:  Lyngbyvej 100, 2100 Copenhagen Ø, just by Ryparken S-train station. DRC has recently moved to a newly renovated multi-tenant house (VOX) with a modern look and shared green canteen.  

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with the agreement between DRC and Lederaftalen between Dansk Arbejdsgiverforening and Lederne (agreement for managers), which can be found here: www.lederne.dk. This is a national position for which local terms and conditions apply.  

We welcome all nationalities to apply for the role. If you do not have the existing right to work in Denmark, DRC will support with applying and paying for a work permit. 

Application process 

If you are motivated by the opportunity to strengthen a global humanitarian organisation through its people, culture and organisational capabilities, we would welcome your application. Korn Ferry is assisting the Danish Refugee Council with the recruitment of the Executive Director, People & Organisation. Please submit your motivated application and CV through the designated recruitment channel. All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV (no longer than four pages) in English. Applications sent by email will not be considered. 

Closing date for applications: Wednesday 11th November 2026  
 

Further information  

For questions regarding the vacancy please contact: Rabea Rehman, Associate | Executive Search at Korn Ferry, E: DRC_PO@KornFerry.com  

For more information about the Danish Refugee Council, please visit our website drc.ngo. 

Danish Refugee Council is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive and positive work environment based on mutual respect for all employees. All applicants are considered for employment regardless of personal characteristics or attributes.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in RNA Biomarkers and Extracellular Vesicle Biology
jobs.description:
Department of Science and Environment, Roskilde University, invites applications as post-doctoral fellow in RNA cell biology from April 1st or as soon as possible thereafter. 

Description of the post-doc project
A fully funded postdoc position (18 months) at Roskilde University in the research group of Professor Dalgaard, funded by Danmarks Frie Forskningsfond (Independent Research Fund Denmark) through the project "Enabling RNA Biomarker Origin Detection by Multiplexing Extracellular Tracing". The project will develop a multiplexed extracellular RNA (exRNA)-tracing platform capable of identifying the cell-of-origin of secreted RNAs in plasma and cell media samples and will demonstrate its use by tracing RNA released by pancreatic islet cells and adipose tissue, both highly relevant to type 2 diabetes (T2D) and obesity. The platform will be valuable for validating novel RNA biomarkers and for discovering RNA-based therapeutic targets in metabolic disease.

Responsibilities and tasks
The postdoc’s work will include research within ExRNA biology, RNA biomarker discovery, and multi-omics profiling, with focus on tracing the cellular origin of secreted RNAs relevant to type 2 diabetes and metabolic disease. In addition, some amount of teaching is also required. 

The ideal candidate is expected to:

• Lead the development and validation of a multiplexed exRNA-tracing platform, based on integration of bio-orthogonal proximity labeling and metabolic RNA labeling systems.
• Perform in vitro and in vivo tracing experiments in pancreatic islet cells, adipose cells, and other relevant cell models to determine the cellular origin of secreted extracellular RNAs and extracellular vesicles (EVs).
• Apply proteomics and small RNA sequencing/omics approaches to characterize the RNA and protein cargo of pancreatic islet- and adipose-derived extracellular vesicles and biofluid samples.
• Analyze and validate candidate RNA biomarkers relevant to T2D and metabolic disease, using plasma and other biofluid samples from relevant cohorts or models.
• Mentor younger or graduate students within the focus of the research project.
Qualifications
Applicants must hold a PhD or equivalent within cell biology, molecular biology, biochemistry, or a related field. Qualifications within the following scientific areas are required:

The ideal candidate has an outstanding track record of accomplishments and a critical mindset. Moreover, an open mentality with focus on research communication, inter-disciplinary curiosity and teamwork will be required to succeed. Moreover, the following qualifications are relevant:

• Certified training in laboratory animal research is required.
• Advanced experimental experience in RNA biology and/or extracellular vesicle (EV) biology is required
• Hands-on experience with proteomics and/or small RNA sequencing or other omics-based biomarker profiling techniques is required.
• Experience with research in metabolic disease, in particular type 2 diabetes or obesity, and/or experience working with pancreatic islets or other metabolically relevant primary cells/tissues, will be highly valuable.
• Experience with publication of original relevant scientific data in peer-reviewed journals will be an advantage.
The ideal candidate should be enterprising and possess good communication skills, be visible and involved in the department’s daily activities, in addition to being willing to engage in disciplinary and interdisciplinary collaboration across the department and with project collaborators.

Assessment
In the assessment of the candidates, consideration will be given to;

• Experience and qualifications as stated above.
• Academic excellence and scientific production relevant to the description above.
• The ability to promote and utilize research results.
• Experience in mentorship and teaching.
• Ability to communicate in written and spoken English.
• Ability to contribute to development of the department’s internal and external cooperations.
The Department of Science and Environment
Department of Science and Environment is one of four departments at Roskilde University. The Department conducts basic and applied research within medical biology, molecular biology, chemistry, physics, environmental sciences, and mathematics. Bachelor programs are offered within these areas, as are interdisciplinary Master programs. The Department’s laboratories are equipped with modern infrastructure and shared state-of-the art instrumentation. This includes recently acquired NMR, mass spectrometry (LC- and GC-MS, including high-resolution measurements and proteomics), and microscopy (AFM, confocal and fluorescence) instruments, GMO class 1 and 2 labs, flow cytometry, NTA, coulter counter, NGS, Q-PCR facilities, pipetting robots, calorimetry (ITC and DSC), chromatography (HPLC), and scattering (DLS, SAXS) instruments.
The post-doctoral position is within the Section of Molecular and Medical Biology: Molecular and Medical Biology | Roskilde University (ruc.dk)
Read more about the Department of Science and Environment at: https://ruc.dk/en/department-science-and-environment

Questions
For further information about the postdoc, please contact Professor Louise Dalgaard (tel. (+45) 4674 2713) or email: ltd@ruc.dk).

Terms of employment
The position is available from 1/5 2027. The employment is full time, and you will refer to Head of Department Susanne Sørensen.

The position will be filled according to the Agreement between the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC) and Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. 

According to the Pay Transparency Directive, the salary ranges for the various job categories at Roskilde University are listed here. 

Application procedure 
After the deadline for applications the Head of Department will shortlist applicants for assessment with assistance from the recruitment committee including the chairperson of the assessment committee.

Shortly after the application deadline all applicants will be notified whether or not their application has been selected for assessment.

The shortlisted applicants will be informed about the composition of the assessment committee, and each applicant will be given the opportunity to comment on the composition of the committee and - later on - their assessment.

Once the recruitment process is completed, all applicants will be informed of the outcome of their application.

Application 
To apply for the position go to www.ruc.dk/en/job/ 

Only applications in English are accepted.

Applications must include:

• Cover letter explaining qualifications, experience and research interests
• CV
• Documentation of education incl. documentation for training in laboratory animal research
• A complete list of publications
• A maximum of 3 relevant scientific works that you want included in the assessment
• If any of the publications that you want included in the assessment are the result of a joint effort, the extent and the nature of your contribution to each individual work must then be clarified in a co-author statement (find template here).
• Teaching portfolio (read more about teaching portfolio at Roskilde University here) 
If any of the publications that you want included in the assessment are the result of a joint effort, the extent and the nature of your contribution to each individual work must then be clarified in a co-author statement (find template here) 

Please submit your application no later than 13th of November 2026. 

Material received after this date will not be taken into consideration.

jobs.occupation: Assistant Professor in Sustainability and Environmental Management
jobs.description:
Department of Science and Environment (DSE), Roskilde University, invites applications for a position as assistant professor in Sustainability and Environmental Management, from January 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is limited for a period of 4 years.

In announcing the position, DSE looks to strengthen its research in environmental sciences within the following fields: Sustainability transitions and circular economy in institutional and healthcare settings, sociotechnical systems analysis, behavioural and consumption analyses, the economic valuation of environmental and health externalities; and the wellbeing economy as a framework connecting these to the circular transition. The Department is interested in applicants who see large-scale, cross-sectoral shifts of this kind - spanning production and consumption systems - as necessary to address today's pressing environmental challenges across the natural- and social-scientific fields represented in the Section for Environmental Dynamics. The position is closely linked to and partly funded by an Innovation Fund Denmark grant for a newly initiated interdisciplinary research project ROUNDS: Rethinking the cost of care – including the cost of externalities in circular transitions. The project links human health risk assessment, ecological economics, and behavioural research to reduce reliance on single-use plastics and textiles in the healthcare sector.

The Department is interested in applicants whose research and teaching profile includes all the above subject areas in combination with an interest in building interdisciplinary research and collaboration on education. The Assistant Professor’s duties will comprise research at a high international level and a strong commitment and contribution to teaching broadly in the environmental science programs at bachelor’s and master’s level. The Assistant Professor will teach in an interdisciplinary environment and engage in problem-oriented project work with extensive student involvement and responsibility.

DSE is one of four departments at Roskilde University. The Department conducts basic and applied research within medical biology, molecular biology, environmental sciences, chemistry, physics, and mathematics. Bachelor and Master programmes are offered within these areas. Research and education within the fields take place in a collaborative and interdisciplinary university environment, also spanning collaboration with the other departments, covering social sciences and humanities, where relevant. The department is organised into four Sections comprising the research and education activities.

The Assistant Professor will be part of the Section for Environmental Dynamics. The Section’s current members primarily have a background within one or more of the fields of aquatic ecology, ecotoxicology, biological production (including aquatic biotechnology), and geochemistry. DSE has a well-established shared infrastructure with state-of-the-art equipment facilities, including field spectroradiometer, Mass-spectrometry (LCMS, GCMS, ICP-MS), CHNS, various microscopy facilities and access to workshops.

Read more about the section at https://ruc.dk/en/research-group/environmental-dynamics

Responsibilities and tasks
The assistant professor’s work will include research, including obligations with regard to publication/scientific communication, and research-based teaching with associated examination obligations within one or more of the fields of the Assistant Professorship and in general activities at the environmental science programme activities.

In addition to research and research-based teaching, the position also requires sharing knowledge with the rest of society - including participation in public debate. To a limited extent, this may also include performance of other activities.

As assistant professor, you are also expected to complete the educational training program for assistant professors at RUC (up to 220 hours). The training programme will give you pedagogical and didactic tools as well as familiarize you with the Roskilde University educational model called Problem oriented project learning (PPL). Applicants are referred to the university’s Faculty expectations (https://ruc.dk/en/working-roskilde-university ) for specifications on the required level of qualifications within research, teaching, networking, fundraising, impact and outreach etc.

The ideal candidate is expected to:

• Lead and further develop research within the circular economy, sustainability transitions, and environmental management in institutional and healthcare settings, including engagement in the research project ROUNDS
• Develop the field of interdisciplinary research by actively collaborating with other scientific fields within the department or at other departments, connecting environmental science with social science and economics
• Contribute to the development of the research profile of the department
• Maintain a significant record of publications
• Collaborate with colleagues in establishing a vibrant research community
• Participate actively in research networks and external research funding activities
• Teach, supervise, and assess students at BSc and MSc levels. This also implies developing the field in relation to teaching
Qualifications
You must hold a PhD degree in Environmental Science or in the interface between the natural and social sciences applied to environmental and sustainability questions. In addition, a documented qualitative and/or interdisciplinary approach to sustainability transitions is required.

Documented research production at international level within one or more of the following scientific areas are required:

• Circular economy and sustainability transitions in institutional or healthcare settings
• Sociotechnical systems theory and analysis of organisational/infrastructural change
• Valuation of environmental and health externalities, including in relation to public procurement
The ideal candidate has:

• Teaching experience within one or more of the fields of the Associate Professor
• A keen interest and experience in project-based, problem-oriented teaching as well as teaching in an interdisciplinary environment
• Documented experience with interdisciplinary research and interdisciplinary collaborations will also be seen as an advantage.
In addition, it will be seen as an advantage if you can contribute to research and teaching within one or more of these areas:

• Environmental management and monitoring
• Political economy of sustainability transitions
• Health systems and behavioural aspects of circular practice
The ideal candidate must be enterprising, possess good communication skills, and be a visible and involved participant in the department’s daily activities, in addition to being willing to engage in disciplinary and interdisciplinary collaboration across the department.

At the time of appointment, successful candidates must master English for academic purposes.

Assessment
In the assessment of the candidates, consideration will be given to:

• Relevance of research topic
• Scientific production at an international level
• Research prospective and the ability to promote and utilise research results
• Experience in teaching and education
• Other academic experience, e.g. from organising research conferences or seminars
• Ability to contribute to development of the department’s internal and external cooperation
Questions
Potential applicants from outside Denmark will find information about life in Denmark (taxation, healthcare etc.) at www.lifeindenmark.borger.dk

For further information about the position, please contact Head of Section Kristian Syberg on tel. (+45) 4674 3776 or e-mail: ksyberg@ruc.dk or Head of Department Susanne Sørensen by email: susa@ruc.dk.

Terms of employment
The employment is on full time, 37 hours per week and in the daily work you will refer to Professor Kristian Syberg. Your head of staff will be Head of Department Susanne Sørensen.

Shortly after the application deadline all applicants will be notified whether or not their application has been selected for assessment.

The shortlisted applicants will be informed about the composition of the assessment committee, and each applicant will be given the opportunity to comment on the composition of the committee and - later on - their assessment.

Once the recruitment process is completed, all applicants will be informed of the outcome of their application.

Application

NG Nordic is a leading provider of circular solutions and environmental services in the Nordics. By transforming waste into valuable resources and removing hazardous substances from the material cycle, we reduce emissions, protect natural ecosystems, and increase access to circular materials. NG Nordic is an important part of the Nordic industrial infrastructure, generating revenue of EUR 1.3 billion with a team of around 3,400 employees and 90 facilities.

Health & Safety Specialist, Nyborg, Denmark

Do you want to be the Safety Shoulder and make a real difference to safety in one of Europe’s most complex industrial environments?

Be the trusted Health & Safety voice in daily operations at NG Nordic’s hazardous waste treatment facility in Nyborg.

As Health & Safety Specialist, you will work close to the operational teams, helping managers and employees turn safety requirements into practical actions. You will be part of a five-person team in Nyborg and work as an integrated partner to Operations.

Nyborg is a Seveso III facility and is described as the EU’s largest hazardous waste treatment plant. Here, health and safety is not simply a compliance exercise: the risks are real, and your work can have a direct impact on people, processes and operational reliability.

Your role combines visible presence in the plant with reporting, statistics, procedures, training and improvement projects. You will advise and challenge Operations constructively, build trust across functions and help ensure a safe, professional operation.

The position is based in Nyborg and requires regular engagement with employees, supervisors and managers throughout the facility.

You will turn safety requirements into practical improvements in daily operations

You will participate in daily and weekly operational meetings, identify and prioritise EHSQ risks, and help the organisation address the issues that matter most. You will balance proactive safety work with administrative responsibilities and timely follow-up.

Your key tasks will include:

• Acting as the Health & Safety partner to Operations, advising managers and employees and participating in daily and weekly operational meetings

• Conducting safety walks, workplace inspections, toolbox talks and awareness activities, and following up on identified risks

• Preparing safety reports, statistics and KPI follow-up, identifying trends and recommending actions

• Developing and implementing practical safety procedures, training programmes, onboarding and contractor inductions

• Supporting risk assessments, audits, investigations and structured root-cause analyses of incidents and near misses

• Driving and prioritising safety improvement projects, monitoring corrective actions and supporting compliance with Danish legislation, internal standards and Seveso-related requirements

Experience from health and safety in industrial operations

We imagine that you have a relevant technical or health and safety qualification and approximately five years or more of experience in a comparable operational environment. Experience from process industry, chemicals, hazardous waste, energy or other high-risk facilities is especially relevant.

You understand occupational health and safety legislation, operational risk assessments, incident investigation, safety management systems and the importance of effective training and documentation. You are comfortable working with reports, statistics and digital tools.

You can translate complex safety requirements into clear, workable solutions. You communicate confidently in Danish and English, both verbally and in writing, and you know how to engage colleagues across functions and organisational levels.

You build credibility through presence, sound judgement and constructive dialogue. You have the natural authority to challenge unsafe practices while maintaining trust and respect, and you are robust enough to handle disagreement and pressure.

You are structured, proactive and able to prioritise competing tasks. You enjoy combining hands-on operational work with analysis, administration and continuous improvement, always keeping the most significant risks in focus.

Interested?

If you want to help create a safer and more professional operation in an environment where safety genuinely matters, we would like to hear from you.

NG Nordic is partnering with Brinch & Partners on this recruitment. For questions about the role, contact Partner Jens Chr. Jensen at +45 7020 2328. Please submit your CV and application in English.

We interview candidates on an ongoing basis.

All enquiries will be treated confidentially.

We want our recruitment process to be fair and inclusive. That is why we do not ask for photos or lengthy cover letters. Instead, we use screening questions to ensure comparable applications. We do, however, ask for gender information to help us ensure good gender balance in the recruitment process.

**About Flatpay

**Flatpay makes card payments simple and fair for small businesses. Marketing is central to how we grow, and we run it as a measurable acquisition engine where curiosity, experimentation and commercial results drive our decisions.

We are looking for an Affiliate & Partnerships Manager to lead our network of affiliates, publishers and lead generation partners across all of our markets.

The role

In six months, affiliate went from zero to one of our most important channels. Now we need someone to take it further.

You like meeting people, spotting opportunities and turning a good conversation into a partnership that performs. You can negotiate a strong deal and still leave the other side wanting to work with you again. And signing is only the start: you will follow each partnership through the funnel, understand what makes it profitable and make it better.

This is a group function. You will report to our Head of Group Marketing, work with colleagues across creative, paid media and analytics, and have real autonomy. We want fewer approval steps, not more. You will need to be self-driven, and in return you will learn a lot across teams and functions.

**What You'll Do

**

• Find new partners. Identify promising affiliates, publishers and lead generation partners, start the conversations and build a pipeline across our markets.

• Negotiate deals that last. Agree pricing, commission structures and terms that support profitable growth for us and a sustainable relationship for them.

• Turn good partners into great ones. Set clear expectations and help partners improve their campaigns, placements and results.

• Look beyond the lead. Follow the journey from lead to booked meeting to customer, and weigh acquisition cost against customer value.

• Make the call. Recommend when to scale, renegotiate, pause or end a partnership.

• Fix what is leaking. Work with partners, the analytics team and sales to find where performance breaks down, then test hypotheses.

• Own the roadmap and reporting. Set the partner roadmap, run onboarding, tracking and commission validation, and report on what the channel delivers.

• Work smarter with AI. Use AI as an assistant to find partners, analyse results and speed up daily work. It supports your judgement and never replaces it.

**How We Work

**

• Quality first, then scale. We would rather have fewer, better leads than many weak ones, but we are not afraid to test. One high-potential partner was trialled in one market and, two months later, was live in five and our biggest partner in the group.

• Shared decisions where it counts. You will set commission models and budgets together with the Head of Group Marketing, so we stay aligned across channels.

**Who You Are

**

Senior Utility Engineer – Plant Engineering (Søborg)

Keep life-changing therapies moving by keeping our utilities running.

Location: Søborg, Denmark. Please note that AGC Biologics does not offer relocation assistance. Applicants must already reside in Denmark or the Greater Malmö area in Sweden.

AGC Biologics is expanding its Utility team in Søborg and is looking for an experienced Senior Utility Engineer with strong expertise in GMP-regulated pharmaceutical water systems. You will play an important role in ensuring the safe, reliable and compliant operation of utility systems that support our 24/7 research, development and production activities.

About the department

The Utility team is responsible for critical utility systems that support production and laboratory operations at our Søborg site. These include pharmaceutical water systems and other essential utilities. You will work closely with Production, QA, Validation, Maintenance and Project teams in a regulated environment where reliability, compliance and patient safety are key priorities.

The role

As Senior Utility Engineer, you will take technical ownership of GMP-critical water systems across the site. This is a hands-on, operational role focused on compliance, troubleshooting, risk reduction and continuous improvement. You will work alongside two skilled technicians who carry out scheduled and unscheduled maintenance, while you focus on system performance, technical oversight and long-term improvements.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Ensuring the stable, compliant and efficient operation of pharmaceutical water systems.

• Taking technical ownership of systems and driving improvements to reliability and performance.

• Maintaining technical documentation, including SOPs, P&IDs and maintenance plans, in line with GMP requirements.

• Leading troubleshooting, root cause analysis, risk assessments and CAPA activities.

• Supporting commissioning, qualification and handover of utility projects to Operations and Maintenance.

• Providing technical input to CAPEX and OPEX projects.

• Representing Utilities during audits and inspections.

• Acting as the senior technical contact for water systems and providing guidance to colleagues across the site.

Most work takes place during regular business hours, although occasional evening or weekend work may be required to support our 24/7 production environment.

Initially, your primary focus will be pharmaceutical water systems. Over time, your responsibilities may expand to include black and clean utilities, allowing you to contribute more broadly across the Utility team.

Experience and competences

We are looking for an experienced Senior Utility Engineer with substantial experience working with pharmaceutical water systems in a GMP-regulated environment.

To succeed in the role, you have:

• An engineering degree in mechanical, electrical or chemical engineering, or a similar field, or an equivalent technical background combined with relevant experience.

• Strong knowledge of pharmaceutical water systems and applicable GMP/GxP requirements.

• Experience with troubleshooting, maintenance and optimisation of technical systems.

• Experience with technical documentation, deviations, CAPAs, risk assessments and regulatory inspections.

• The ability to take technical ownership, solve complex problems and drive improvements independently.

• The ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams and communicate technical information clearly.

Experience with GMP utilities, project handovers, black and clean utilities, regulatory audits and mentoring colleagues is an advantage.

As a person, you are

You are proactive, independent and comfortable taking ownership of your responsibilities. You are structured and solution-oriented, with a strong focus on quality and compliance. You communicate clearly, collaborate effectively across teams and enjoy sharing knowledge with colleagues. You are comfortable balancing operational priorities with technical documentation and continuous improvement.

AGC offers

At AGC Biologics, you will work with critical utility systems in a dynamic pharmaceutical production environment. You will join a collaborative team where knowledge sharing, ownership and practical problem-solving are valued. The role offers the opportunity to develop your technical expertise and contribute to the reliable operation of systems that support our production activities around the clock.

How to apply

Please submit your application and CV through the AGC Biologics career site. We do not accept applications by email.

Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, and we reserve the right to close the vacancy before the deadline if a suitable candidate is found.

Please note that AGC Biologics does not offer relocation assistance. Applicants must already reside in Denmark or the Greater Malmö area in Sweden.

We look forward to receiving your application!

Who We Are

AGC Biologics is a global Contract Development and Manufacturing Organization with a strong presence in Denmark. From our Søborg site, we develop and manufacture life‑changing advanced biologics for some of the world’s most innovative pharmaceutical companies. Together with our team members across Europe, the U.S., and Japan, we deliver development and manufacturing of mammalian and microbial-based therapeutic proteins, plasmid DNA (pDNA), messenger RNA (mRNA), viral vectors, and genetically engineered cells therapies. Across our global network, we are united by one mission: To work side by side with our customers in order to improve patients’ lives by bringing new biopharmaceuticals to market.

jobs.occupation: Clinical position as staff specialist combined with a clinical associate professorship (research) in Paediatrics- Børn og Unge, Sjællands Universitetshospital
jobs.description:
A clinical position as staff specialist of Paediatrics at the Department of Paediatrics and Adolescent Medicine at Zealand University Hospital is open for appointment from as soon as possible.

The position as staff specialist is combined with a 5-year externally funded position as clinical associate professor (research) in Paediatrics at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen.

With this new position the Department of Paediatrics and Adolescent Medicine, Zealand University Hospital wishes to strengthen the leadership in clinical research and teaching in collaboration with the University of Copenhagen.

It is a requirement that the applicant is accepted for appointment of both the clinical associate professorship (research) and the clinical position.

About the Department

The Department of Paediatrics and Adolescent Medicine at Zealand University Hospital is a well-established clinical and research-active department with sites in Roskilde (planned move to Køge 2028) and Nykøbing Falster. The department provides comprehensive care across the full spectrum of paediatrics, including specialised services within paediatric endocrinology and the management of childhood diabetes.

The treatment of childhood diabetes in Region Zealand is organised across multiple sites, enabling strong cross-site collaboration and the development of shared clinical pathways. The department works closely with Steno Diabetes Center Zealand and collaborates with paediatric departments both within and beyond the region.

The department offers a dynamic research environment with a focus on strengthening clinical research, including dedicated research within childhood diabetes. This field involves distinct clinical and developmental considerations compared to adult diabetes, and research activities address treatment outcomes, patient development, quality of life and health equality.

Teaching and supervision of medical students and junior doctors are integral parts of the department’s activities, and there is a strong emphasis on developing future clinicians and clinical researchers.

Qualifications:

Applicants for a position as staff specialist must be board-certified specialist in Paediatrics.

Conditions:

In order to be considered, the applicant must send an application to both the Faculty (the clinical associate professorship (research)) and to the hospital (the clinical position) cf. the simultaneously advertised position of the clinical associate professorship (research). Appointment is conditioned by the fact that the applicant obtains both positions. This also applies to the applicants who are already employed as staff specialists at Zealand University Hospital.

Salary and conditions of employment as staff specialist are as agreed between the Danish Regions and the Danish Association of Medical Specialists and between the Capital Region/Region Zealand and University of Copenhagen.

As clinical associate professor (research) at least 50 % of the working time will be allocated to academic tasks (e.g. research, teaching, evaluation tasks and communication with the public) in agreement with the Head of Department of Clinical Medicine at the University of Copenhagen. The remaining time will be allocated for clinical work in agreement with the head of Department of Paediatrics and Adolescent Medicine.

Application procedure:

The application must include the following:

• Curriculum Vitae and a complete list of publications

• A description of how the applicant is qualified as

- Clinical expert

- Communicator

- Collaborator

- Manager/administrator/organizer

- Health advocate

- Scholar/researcher/teacher, professional

For more information please refer to https://sundhedsstyrelsen.dk/en/news/2013/the-seven-roles-of-physicians.

For applicants with a foreign license also a copy of the authorization certificate for specialist in Paediatrics recognition.

The closing date for applications is 30.11.2026.

Further information:

For further information please contact Head of Department of Paediatrics and Adolescent Medicine, Malene Boas, mboa@regionsjaelland.dk

The advertisement for the clinical associate professorship (research) is available from the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen

171819 Clinical Associate Professor (Research) of Paediatrics (Fixed-term, 5 years)

Sjællands Universitetshospital er Danmarks nyeste universitetshospital med aktiviteter i Køge, Roskilde og Nykøbing F. Vi er et modigt og udadvendt universitetshospital, hvor vi hver dag arbejder for at skabe et sammenhængende sundhedsvæsen og større lighed i sundhed for borgerne i regionen.

Vores optageområde er præget af flere borgere med kronisk sygdom og sociale udfordringer end landsgennemsnittet. Derfor arbejder vi målrettet med innovation, nye samarbejdsformer og løsninger, der bringer behandling tættere på borgerne.

Hos os bliver du en del af en ambitiøs arbejdsplads, hvor samarbejde på tværs, høj faglighed og løbende forbedringer er en naturlig del af hverdagen. Vores ledelsesværdier er nytænkning, følgeskab, ordentlighed og fællesskab, og de sætter retning for, hvordan vi arbejder, udvikler os og skaber gode resultater – for både borgere og medarbejdere.

This is a senior individual-contributor role with broad technical responsibility and influence across functions and projects. You will lead technical workstreams and mentor experienced engineers without formal line-management responsibility.

**What You Will Do

**Working closely with Manufacturing, Engineering, Automation, Quality, Validation, and external partners, you will:

• Lead bioprocess design and optimization: Set the technical direction for upstream and downstream processes, purification, bulk formulation, and sterile transfers. Use process knowledge, modelling, and manufacturing data to improve yield, capacity, reliability, and product quality.

• Shape automation and control strategies: Translate process needs into requirements for PLC/DCS and SCADA systems, recipes, sequences, interlocks, and alarms. Ensure solutions support effective process control, data integrity, and reliable operation.

• Provide technical leadership for filtration: Define filter selection, sizing, validation, and integrity-testing strategies for liquid and gas systems. Lead investigations into filter failures, pressure deviations, and performance issues.

• Guide equipment and system design: Review and approve tanks, piping, pumps, valves, and instrumentation, including hydraulic calculations, pressure distribution, and pressure-testing strategies. Lead technical decisions for Cleaning-in-Place and Sterilization-in-Place (CIP/SIP) systems.

• Deliver projects and technology transfers: Lead process engineering activities from concept and vendor selection through factory and site acceptance testing, commissioning, qualification, process validation, and handover to operations.

• Strengthen technical standards and compliance: Resolve complex investigations, support change controls and CAPAs, and represent engineering during audits and inspections. Establish reusable design standards and share knowledge across projects and teams.

**What You Bring

**You have a master’s degree or PhD in Bioengineering, Biochemical or Chemical Engineering, Biotechnology, Mechanical Engineering, or a closely related discipline.

You bring substantial industrial experience, typically 15 years or more, including at least 10 years within pharmaceutical, biotechnology or vaccine manufacturing.

Your experience includes:

• Leading complex engineering projects as a lead engineer or technical authority, with hands-on expertise in bioprocess development, scale-up, commercial manufacturing, and lifecycle management.

• Integrating process equipment with automation and SCADA systems, including control strategies, computerized-system validation, and data integrity.

• Designing and validating filtration systems, including filter integrity testing and pressure/flow troubleshooting.

• Working with hygienic tanks and piping, hydraulic calculations, pressure testing, CIP/SIP, and contamination control.

• Leading commissioning, qualification, process validation, Process Performance Qualification, and technology transfer, supported by a strong understanding of GMP and quality risk management.

• Setting technical standards, mentoring experienced engineers, and influencing decisions across functions without relying on formal authority.

**How You Work

**You combine scientific depth with practical engineering judgement. You can move from detailed technical analysis to clear recommendations that help colleagues and leaders make informed decisions.

You take ownership, challenge assumptions constructively, and remain focused when problems span multiple systems or disciplines. Whether working with operators, specialists, suppliers, or senior stakeholders, you communicate clearly and build trust through sound decisions and consistent follow-through.

You also enjoy developing others. Sharing expertise, coaching colleagues, and creating common standards are natural parts of how you work.

**Why join Bavarian Nordic?

**At Bavarian Nordic, we work to protect lives through vaccines. In this role, you will help build and improve the manufacturing capabilities that make that purpose possible.

You will have the opportunity to influence major technical decisions, strengthen engineering practices, and see your work translate into measurable improvements in manufacturing performance and reliable supply.

Our values—Persisting Pioneers, Embracing Change, and Boosted by the Team—shape how we collaborate and solve challenges. For the right candidate, sustained performance may open opportunities for broader engineering leadership or formal people management.

**Ready to shape the future of our Drug Substance manufacturing?

**We look forward to receiving your application and learning how your technical expertise and leadership could strengthen Bavarian Nordic.
